sections.skill: Compare federal and private student loans and calculate interest that accrues during school

questions.prompt: Kira borrows a $5,500 unsubsidized loan at 6%. Interest builds for 4 years while she is in school. How much simple interest accrues?
questions.intro: On a Direct Unsubsidized Loan, interest accrues (builds) from the day the money is paid out, even during school. Simple interest = principal × rate × time.
questions.topic: Student loans: federal, private, and interest
sources: Federal Student Aid (Loan types): Interest on Direct Subsidized Loans is paid by the government while the student is in school at least half-time; Direct Unsubsidized Loans accrue interest from disbursement. Federal loan rates are fixed for the life of each loan and set each year. (https://studentaid.gov/understand-aid/types/loans)

CFPB (Private student loans): Private student loans may have variable rates, require a cosigner, and lack federal protections such as income-driven repayment. (https://www.consumerfinance.gov/consumer-tools/student-loans/)

questions.prompt: Kira's $5,500 loan has $1,320 of unpaid interest that is added to the balance when repayment begins. What is the new balance?
questions.intro: When unpaid interest is added to the principal, it is "capitalized." Future interest is then charged on the larger balance.

questions.prompt: What is the key difference between subsidized and unsubsidized federal loans?

choices.text: Only unsubsidized loans must be repaid
Who pays the interest during school
Subsidized loans come from private banks
Unsubsidized loans have no interest at all

questions.correct_answer: Who pays the interest during school
questions.intro: For Direct Subsidized Loans (need-based), the government pays the interest while the student is in school at least half-time. For unsubsidized loans, the student is responsible for all interest.
questions.feedback: Subsidized: government pays in-school interest. Unsubsidized: interest accrues.

questions.prompt: Which is usually true of private student loans compared with federal ones?

choices.text: They always have a lower fixed rate than federal loans
They include income-driven repayment by law
They need no credit check at all
They may need a cosigner

questions.intro: Federal loans have fixed rates set each year and protections such as income-driven repayment and deferment. Private loans depend on credit, often need a cosigner, may have variable rates, and have fewer protections.
questions.feedback: Private loans depend on credit and often need a cosigner.
